attribution.note: Zitron's own words in his own post, written in his own voice.

semantics.note: It keeps 'unquestionably' and 'everybody'. It also keeps the claim that Google's moves are hurting Google, and that this led to Bing's opening. 'Hyper-optimizing search' is slightly narrower than 'these moves', which also covers ads and SEO content, but the contract restores that wider scope. Firm causal claim.

contract.note: The plain reading is ordinary and fair. 'Hurting' means harm to search usefulness or standing, with no financial loss required, and 'everybody' is read as rhetorical. The support condition rightly requires evidence of causation beyond launch publicity.

evidence.note: Contemporary TIME coverage dated 2023-02-08. It establishes the major-headlines part only. The performance claims come from Microsoft, and it says nothing on whether Google's choices caused the opening.
Independent ACSI survey (Jul 2021–Jun 2022) shows Google satisfaction fell 5% to 75. It does not tie the drop to the named changes or link it to Bing's reception.
Microsoft's own disclosure confirms the 2023-02-07 launch. It is not independent evidence of harm to Google or of user preference.

WIRED launch report, which also counts as major coverage. Microsoft admits hallucinations are unsolved. This qualifies the 'service everybody wished' framing but does not test or disprove the causal link.

reviews.rationale: The headlines part is backed by TIME and WIRED coverage from the launch. The core causal claim, that Google's own moves harmed it and opened the way for Bing, is not established. ACSI shows Google satisfaction falling but does not isolate the cause, and nothing links that harm to Bing's reception apart from general AI hype. Nothing directly disproves the link either. The contract needs both parts, so the outcome stays unresolved.
